featured_reviews.review_text:
BLUE’S Thai Kitchen serves excellent Thai food, and it’s a place I genuinely love. I’ve visited multiple times over the last 4–5 years, and the food quality has remained consistently great. Chef Loima at times chats and recommends some dishes to try.

The restaurant is quite small, with around six tables accommodating roughly 20 people, so it can feel cramped. Despite this, the service is super fast, and the team works efficiently to manage the crowd.

One piece of feedback, the owner (often present) tends to stand very close to tables or hover around, which can feel uncomfortable. Regardless of the waiting outside, customers come for the experience and should be allowed to sit, relax, and enjoy their meal without feeling rushed or watched or someone being very direct or rude.

Apart from this, everything else is excellent. Still a highly recommended spot for authentic Thai food.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Locomo Express Hostel recommended Khoa Piyo Restaurant, and I visited there alone for dinner.

I asked for Kingfisher Ultra, and the manager initially confirmed that it was available. However, after a few minutes, another staff member came and informed me that it was not available and that only other brands were in stock. I then requested Budweiser, which was served.

The beer was served without any complimentary snacks like nuts or chips. I also had to ask separately for drinking water, whereas normally water is brought to the table automatically for customers.

I ordered chicken biryani, which was just okay.

After finishing my meal, I requested the bill, and the brought the QR code for payment. However, the manager took the bill from my hand with visible irritation, which felt uncomfortable and unprofessional.

When I was leaving, no staff member was present at the door to open it or even acknowledge me. Two staff members were sitting near the entrance, talking to each other, but there was no courtesy, greeting, or farewell shown.

Overall, I felt the service lacked basic hospitality, professionalism, and customer respect. I hope the management will take this feedback positively and improve their service standards.

featured_reviews.name: Danish Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Toooo Goooddd!!! This place offers so many cuisines that your mind will be confused right from the start. It includes everything from indian and sindhi to mexican, italian and arabic; also offers asian and exotic food items such as fondues. Has a seating area on entry and on the first floor too. Coming to my experience here, it was a mixed review since we had problems related to the air-conditioner and it's management. We sat on the first floor and there's a staircase to reach there. Ambience at both the levels is great and superb!! While the ambience was great, the air-conditioner was equally unrewarding since they weren't working properly. We even reported that to the staff but they said that they already know it's not working and started pretending that they've called the technicians at 4 in the evening the same day!! So even after coming through such scorching heat outside, the inside wasn't much different. Finally after shifting places thrice, we found a spot where cool air could be felt! Apart from all this the food was sooo yummy, fresh and adequate in quantity that my brain didn't have any other issue to focus on!🙌
Food review-
1.Cream of Tomato with Basil soup- 5/5 for quantity, 5/5 for taste. Also they serve extra croutons if asked for!!🤭
2. Pahadi paneer tikka- 5/5 for quantity, 5/5 for taste. The paneer pieces were soooo soft and felt really fresh!!
3. Lasagne Ala Napolitano- 3/5 for quantity, 4/5 for taste. Was less in quantity as compared to other places i've had lasagne. Less cheesy as per the standard flavour of lasagne.
4. Dum aloo punjabi- 10/5 for quantity, 10/5 for taste. Reallly reallly very goood in everythinggg from quantity to taste to the dum aloo pieces. Usually 1 potato is provided but here 2 were provided and it's masala and gravy was also soo yummm!!!😋
5. Butter kulcha- 5/5 for taste. Soft, fresshhhh and buttery!!
6. Chinese sizzler- 1/5 for quantity and 1/5 for taste. Typically a chinese sizzler consists of rice, noodles, manchurian balls, chinese gravy and sautéd veggies. But this consisted just of rice, noodles and sautéd veggies. There were no manchurian balls nor there was any gravy which adds to the taste in sizzlers. REALLY A BIG WASTE OF MONEY, I WOULDN'T RECOMMEND YOU TO ORDER ANY SIZZLER AFTER TRYING THIS ONE AS THIS WAS OVERPRICED AS COMPARED TO ANY OTHER PLACE.
7. Basil Citrus Breeze Margarita- 5/5 for look, 3/5 for taste. Looks too fancy and delicious but is just okay. Full of ice and  essence. Won't matter if you don't try this.

featured_reviews.name: amin shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
📍 Kuai Kitchen – Khar West, Mumbai
🍱 Location: Shop No. 3/4, Mangal Bhavna, Khar Pali Rd, Khar West, Mumbai 400052
If you're a fan of sushi, dim sum, and pan-Asian cuisine, Kuai Kitchen is the place to be! The ambience here is aesthetic and welcoming, with both indoor and outdoor dining options that make it a perfect spot for a cozy meal or a catch-up with friends.
We started off with some refreshing mocktails — I tried the Martini mocktail, which was super refreshing and full of flavor. My brother went for the Panda Passion, and not only did it taste amazing, but the presentation was on point too!
Here’s what we ordered and absolutely loved:
🍤 Dynamite Prawns – perfectly crispy and packed with flavor.
🥟 Spicy Chicken Dumplings – delicious, with a rich, flavorful filling and great presentation.
🍣 Volcano Prawn Tempura Roll Sushi – visually stunning and tasted just as good as it looked.
🍗 Chicken with Chilli Oil and Spring Onion – bold flavors with a nice kick.
🍚 Blue Butter Japanese Fried Rice (Chicken) – cooked to perfection, flavorful, and unique in taste.
And finally, to end on a sweet note:
🍫 Labubu Chocolate Bao – a warm, gooey dessert bao that was absolutely mouthwatering!
✨ The service was top-notch. The staff were attentive and helpful, and the manager personally guided us through the menu. Every dish was presented beautifully, and the quality was consistent throughout.
💯 Overall: 10/10 Experience
Highly recommended for all lovers of Thai, Asian, sushi, and dim sum. Add this place to your food bucket list — you won't regret it!

featured_reviews.name: aditya mathur
featured_reviews.review_text:
FAKE HYPE. AVOID visit. Very disappointed. Nothing special atall. Just a mediocre pan Asia joint . Lets get straight to it. Came here as i read good reviews online but sadly it was all wrong.
We were a party of 10 who went here on a Saturday night.
Cons :
1. No valet when we arrived. Had to look for parking for 15 mins.
2. Less than enthusiastic staff and thats putting lightly.
3. Small place so getting a seating inside might be difficult.
4. Lotus stem and teriyaki bao were soo sweet that it felt like eating desert. This was conveyed to the management for feedback.
5. Tatse and portion of the dishes do not justify the its cost. Too steep for the kind of mideocre food available.
6. Steamed rice was undercooked and left untouched. We had given up by this time and resorted to looking elsewhere for dinner party 2 .
7. No alcohol. Alcohol would have helped in stuffing down some of the itmes we ordered or atleast numb our taste buds enough to appreciate the food.
Pros :
1. Ambience is neat and cosy.
2. The sushi was very well made and we all enjoyed it.
3. The menu is well curated with good variety of both veg and non veg options.
I dont know if this was a one off case or our choice of items was poor or the staff was overwhelmed on a Saturday night or was it just the normal standard here but the fact remains that we were truly disappointed 😔 by the experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a fan of bold flavors and comforting desi Chinese, Fat Kong is the kind of place that satisfies every craving with just the right hit of spice, crunch, and umami.

Crispy Chicken:
This dish was a knockout. The chicken pieces were perfectly battered—thin, golden, and fried to a shatteringly crisp texture. The outside had that addictive crunch, while the inside stayed juicy and tender. Tossed in a sticky, mildly spicy glaze with hints of garlic, soy, and chili, it was garnished with spring onions and sesame seeds, making it hard to stop at just one piece.

Chicken Triple Rice & Schezwan Noodles:
The Chicken Triple Rice was a full-on flavor bomb—a mix of fried rice and schezwan gravy poured generously on top, loaded with chopped veggies, chicken chunks, and a fried egg to top it all off. It was hearty, spicy, and soul-satisfying in that uniquely desi-Chinese way.

The Schezwan Noodles had a perfect wok-char (you know that smoky “wok hei” touch), with the right chewiness and a punchy garlic-chili flavor that didn’t overpower. Again, the chicken pieces were soft and well-seasoned, blending nicely with the heat of the schezwan sauce and the crunch of stir-fried vegetables.

It's with a heavy heart that I have to give 2 stars to a restaurant which was one of my favourites earlier on. Before the restaurant was located on SV Road Opposite Dynasty restaurant and everything was top class. It was one of those restaurants where we visited every weekend and it was always full so we had to wait 15 to 20 mins to get a table, and it was worth the wait.

So after around a decade I decided to revisit this restaurant for nostalgia and to try their iconic starters which made me drool earlier on.

So they are having two outlets now Jogeshwari and Khar, I visited the Khar outlet and was happy to see the restaurant maintaining their yellow and red colour theme. I was the only one present in their restaurant and was greeted by Akshay the person managing this outlet.

After requesting that I wish to try 2 dishes he was kind enough to give me 1/2 portion of my favourite Chicken Lollipop Hakka Style and Full portion of Crispy Spinach Chicken.

As soon as the lollipops were served the aroma transported me to the old era it was so beautiful and they have done well to maintain their taste as it was before.

But now comes the sad part, I got a piece of plastic spoon in my mouth while having the dish and was angry, disappointed and sad. I was advised by some of my friends that I should avoid the restaurant as it's not maintained the same way like before, but still I decided to try and I was like this is the end of Fatkongs for me.

I requested the Manager to not charge me for this dish and speak to the owner regarding this but he was helpless and they decided not to take away the charges.

Even though this incident took place I still ate the second dish Crispy Spinach Chicken, but it was nowhere close to the one which I used to eat before. The spinach didn't seem fresh and the chicken had a thick coating and wasn't good. So with a heavy heart I left the restaurant putting down a message to the owner who did give me a call and tried to give explanation and reasoning, though admitting that it wasn't right. But somehow I didn't feel like trying this restaurant again.

featured_reviews.name: Riddhiman Chanda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Linking Road in Bandra is home to some of the best food in the city, and one of the best asian joints in the place is The fatty Bao. It has a modern, chic vibe crossed with a vibrant and sassy decor, perfect for a date night, or for a hangout sesh with friends.

The decor feels inspired by Malay/Singaporean cafes, with a lot of the artwork depicting the same, and it comes off pretty well. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, though the indoor seating is a bit cramped, but that's mostly fine. They do have a small bar serving the usual suspects, as well as some of their own stuff.

While I didn't get to order a large chunk of their menu, whatever I had was pretty great. Their name is definitely apt, as the baos I got were plump and pillowy, and the filling was perfect. I got the pork char siu baos, and the pork was fatty and melt in your mouth, complimented nicely by a slice of raw apple, giving it a fruity kick. Every Bao order comes with two, making it perfect for date night.

I also got their raw papaya salad, which was one of the best renditions of the dish I've eaten in Mumbai. It was tangy, sweet and spicy in just the right amounts, and wasn't just a refreshing palate cleanser, but a great meal by itself. It's also a very generous portion making it great for sharing.

The last thing I got were Chicken and asparagus dumplings, which didn't impress me as much, as I've had better dumplings in the same price range. They weren't bad but not particularly great either. The filling was generous, but it lacked in flavor. For 6 pieces, it was not the best value, and I recommend trying other dumplings, or avoiding dumplings all together.

Overall, I would rate both the Char Siu Bao and the Papaya Salad a solid 9/10, and the dumplings about a 6.5/10. Definitely go for their baos( pretty obvious given their name).

The service was fine, but they do tend to ignore the smaller tables and focus on the bigger groups, and it was also pretty busy on the day I visited. But I did see other tables also not receiving food at the proper times, so I'd rate the service a little lower, like a 6/10. Definitely could do with some improvement.

The Fatty Bao definitely ticks a lot of the boxes, though they do miss a little bit in their service, and cocktail variety, though I did not have the opportunity to try it. However, they more than make up for it with their snazzy decor and contemporary vibe, along with some pretty great food. I highly recommend checking the place out if you're out shopping in Linking Road and need to grab some lunch or dinner. You're definitely gonna be leaving a happy and fatty bao when you're done.

Final rating- 8.5/10, definitely recommend.

featured_reviews.name: Hania
featured_reviews.review_text:
Peach Ice Tea
Peach Iced Tea is a refreshing burst of flavor in every sip.

Kalimiri Cheddar Broccoli
From the moment the dish arrives, the vibrant green of the broccoli is contrasted beautifully by the creamy richness of the cheddar cheese, infused with the subtle yet captivating warmth of kalimiri (black pepper). The aroma is inviting—cheesy, slightly spicy, and earthy.The broccoli retains a nice crunch, providing a fresh, earthy base to the dish. The cheddar is indulgently smooth, delivering a familiar, comforting creaminess. But what sets this dish apart is the kalimiri. The black pepper’s spice gently lingers, balancing the richness of the cheese with a subtle heat. The tender yet slightly crisp broccoli pairs wonderfully with the velvety melted cheddar. Perfect for those looking for something familiar with a hint of spice. However, the spice of cardamom was overpowered and sat on tongue, so every bite was full of cardamom, which made the next dishes taste like it too.

Tiranga Kofte
Visually, the Tiranga Kofte presents itself well, with three distinct layers symbolizing the colours of the Indian flag. The presentation is appealing and sets high expectations for a flavourful experience. However, the dish's appearance slightly outweighs its taste. The kofte has a decent blend of spices, though the flavours don’t quite come together as cohesively as expected. Each layer brings something different—the green layer offers a mild herbiness, the white layer is a bit bland, and the orange section has a touch of heat. However, the balance between them feels uneven, with the spices not blending as harmoniously as they should.
Since the appetizer had cardamom hint which was overpowering, the outer layer green part of kofta also felt it had cardamom which wasn’t pleasant on tongue.

Amritsari Kulcha
The Amritsari-styled kulcha is a delightful treat. Each bite offers a perfect blend of crispy exterior and soft, flavorful interior. The traditional stuffing of spiced potatoes and herbs is well-seasoned, providing a hearty and satisfying taste

Lachha Paratha
The Lachha Paratha is a standout with its perfectly layered, crispy texture. Each bite reveals a delightful combination of flaky. Though they forgot to add butter because it was some miscommunication, It was perfect size not big not small.

Tadkewali Dal
Tadkewali Dal delivers a heartwarming, flavorful experience. The smoky aroma from the tadka (tempering) hits you immediately, preparing your senses for a rich and comforting dish. The lentils are cooked to perfection—and well-spiced. The tadka of ghee, cumin, garlic, and chilies adds depth, bringing a savory warmth to every bite. Each spoonful is a harmonious blend of velvety dal and robust, fragrant spices. It’s a perfect dish for anyone seeking bold yet balanced flavors in a simple, soul-satisfying homely meal.

Jeera rice
Jeera Rice is simplicity at its finest. The delicate aroma of cumin wafts through each grain, giving the rice a warm, earthy fragrance. The cumin seeds add a subtle crunch and a toasted, nutty flavor that complements the perfectly cooked, fluffy rice.

Halwa (Complementary)
Rich and buttery, each spoonful melts in your mouth, releasing a wave of sweetness that’s perfectly balanced with hints of cardamom. The texture is smooth yet slightly grainy, with bursts of flavor from the roasted nuts scattered throughout.

Hospitality
The hospitality at this restaurant is exceptional. From the moment we walked in, the staff was warm, attentive, and welcoming. They ensured every detail was taken care of, making us feel comfortable and valued throughout the meal. Service was prompt, yet never rushed, with the team showing genuine care in their recommendations and interactions. Their professionalism, combined with friendly smiles, truly elevated our experience. Ashish and Prasad served great hospitality to us.

Ambience
The ambience of Rasoi strikes the perfect balance between luxury and comfort. The decor is elegant yet welcoming, with soft lighting and tasteful accents that create a warm, inviting atmosphere

featured_reviews.name: Rahil Kotadia
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place by the Bawa Hotels Group is a good option if you’re in the mood for Punjabi food, just don’t walk in expecting completely authentic flavours. The taste is slightly toned down, but if you set your expectations right, you’ll actually enjoy the food.

The menu is quite well done, and the meal box options are a big plus. Makes ordering super easy without having to overthink or pick too many individual items.

Their parathas are definitely worth trying—served nicely with curd. Do ask for white butter separately though, as it’s not given by default and really makes a difference. The lassi is a must-have here, easily one of the better things on the menu.

Also, a special mention for the Kalimiri chicken shorba. It’s not on the menu, but if they have it, don’t miss it—it’s genuinely very good.

Ambience is nice and comfortable, so no complaints there. Service, however, is quite slow and needs serious improvement, which can get a bit frustrating.

Parking is another issue—since it’s close to the railway station, the area is always crowded and finding a spot is tough. Better to plan that in advance.

Overall, a good place to chill and enjoy a meal, as long as you’re okay overlooking the service and parking hassles.

featured_reviews.review_text:

My absolute favourites were their creamy butter chicken, soft and flavourful chhole kulcha, and the super refreshing lassi that perfectly balanced the spices. Every dish tasted like it was made with love and tradition. If you’re craving authentic Punjabi flavours with a celebratory twist, this is the place to be — go check it out and treat yourself to a hearty, happy meal!

For my mains I got the Mutton Beliram (don’t why it’s called that) which was nice and spicy, along with a roomali roti. I’d recommend ordering a naan instead - lots of very moorish sauce to lap up! Got some Jal Jeera with soda to wash it down (not sure about the boondi). Finished off with some Gulabjamun - there is definitely a hint of “Gulab” there! And just look at those soft, pillowy, inviting mounds. 😆

Overall Bawa Kitchen echoes the punjabi ethos when it comes to food. It’s definitely a place I’d recommend and visit again!

The food, overall, was really good and definitely amps up the experience. That said, I’d love to see a wider variety of sushi and noodle dishes on the menu. Definitely a spot I’d come back to (and happily recommend) when I’m in the mood for a relaxed, date-night style dinner.

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Some restaurants become popular, while others become part of a city’s collective memory. Paul’s Chinese in Dadar firmly belongs to the latter category. For decades, it has been serving generations of Mumbaikars, earning a reputation that stretches from local food lovers to cricketing legend Sachin Tendulkar himself. Yet despite its fame, Paul’s has retained the authenticity and soul that made it a neighbourhood favourite in the first place.
The food here is everything Mumbai-style Chinese should be bold, comforting, flavourful, and immensely satisfying. Every dish arrives packed with the unmistakable aromas and flavours that have made Paul’s an institution.
The legendary Chicken Chopper Rice is an absolute masterpiece and a must-order. Hearty, indulgent, and loaded with flavour, it perfectly captures the restaurant’s signature style. Equally impressive is the Triple Rice, a beloved classic that delivers the perfect balance of rice, noodles, gravy, and textures in every bite. The Hakka Noodles are expertly prepared, with just the right amount of wok hei and seasoning that keeps you reaching for more.
One of the highlights of the meal was undoubtedly the Paul’s Special Non-Veg Box, a generous feast that showcases the kitchen’s greatest hits in one satisfying package. The Veg Box is equally impressive and proves that vegetarian diners are in for just as memorable an experience.
The starters deserve special applause. Whether it’s the succulent chicken preparations, fresh seafood delicacies, or the surprisingly delicious vegetarian offerings, every dish demonstrates why Paul’s continues to command such a loyal following. The seafood is particularly noteworthy… fresh, perfectly cooked, and packed with flavour without being overwhelmed by sauces.
Beyond the food, the service reflects the warmth of a family-run legacy. The staff are courteous, attentive, and efficient, handling the bustling crowds with ease while ensuring guests feel welcome and comfortable. There is a sense of familiarity and genuine hospitality that is increasingly rare in today’s dining scene.
What makes Paul’s truly special is the legacy it carries. This is not just a restaurant; it is a Mumbai institution. Countless college students, office-goers, families, late-night food seekers, and loyal regulars have grown up eating here. The fact that it remains a favourite across generations is perhaps the greatest testament to its quality and consistency.
In a city overflowing with new restaurants and fleeting food trends, Paul’s Chinese continues to stand tall because it understands something timeless: great food, generous portions, warm service, and consistency never go out of style.
Whether you’re a first-time visitor or a lifelong regular, a meal at Paul’s feels like reconnecting with an old friend. A true Dadar legend and one of Mumbai’s most iconic Chinese dining destinations.

featured_reviews.name: Sarbjeet Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Paul Chinese in Matunga West is a go-to spot for classic Indo-Chinese food that’s flavorful, affordable, and filling. The place has a simple, no-frills setup focused entirely on serving fast, tasty meals.

I tried the Chicken Manchurian (Dry), Veg Fried Rice, and Schezwan Noodles. The Chicken Manchurian was the standout—perfectly cooked with a bold, tangy-spicy sauce. The Veg Fried Rice was light and well-balanced, while the Schezwan Noodles, though spicy, could’ve used a bit more flavor depth.

Service is quick and efficient, even when it’s busy. Portion sizes are generous and the pricing is student-friendly. If you're in Matunga West and craving Indo-Chinese, this place won’t disappoint.

Highlights:

Tasty, classic Indo-Chinese dishes

Fast service

Great portion size and value for money

Room for Improvement:

Schezwan dishes could use more flavor complexity

Ambience is basic—more focused on function than feel

Overall, a reliable and satisfying option for quick Chinese meals in the area.

featured_reviews.name: viraj pai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Paul Chinese is a fairly ordinary Chinese eatery with a basic setup. The restaurant has two floors—while the upper floor is air-conditioned, it has a very low ceiling which requires you to bend while walking. The ground floor, on the other hand, is non-AC and offers minimal comfort.
We ordered Chicken Lollipop with gravy, Triple Schezwan Fried Rice, and Chopper Rice for three people. The Chicken Lollipop was decent but nothing exceptional. The Triple Schezwan Fried Rice came with a red-colored gravy that looked artificial and lacked any real flavor. The dish had a strong eggy smell, which was quite off-putting. The Chopper Rice was bland, with barely any vegetables, and felt underwhelming in both taste and presentation.

We decided to try this place after watching a positive review on YouTube. However, our experience was disappointing and makes us question the authenticity of such glowing reviews, which may very well be paid promotions. Dining here felt like a gamble that, unfortunately, didn’t pay off—leaving us with an unpleasant aftertaste, both literally and figuratively.
